deities: Sri Unnikrishna (infant form of Krishna; presiding deity)
Goddess Bhadrakali / Bhagavathy (worshipped with equal ardour, shrine left of Krishna)
Lord Ganesha (sub-shrine, plus a Ganesha sub-temple behind the main temple)
festivals: Thrissur Pooram (Medam, April-May; the temple is one of the two dominant participants with Paramekkavu; Madathilvaravu procession of Bhagavathy and Krishna to Vadakkunnathan Temple)

history.dynasty: Kochi royal family (present structure attributed to Sakthan Thampuran, i.e., Raja Rama Varma IX, 18th century)
history.period: 16th-century origins at Edakkalathur; present Thrissur structure attributed to the 18th century
history.summary: The Thiruvambady Temple, dedicated to Unnikrishna (infant Krishna), began at Edakkalathur, about 20 km away. Legend says that in the 16th century, amid communal strife in the village (triggered by a romance between a Moose-family girl and a man of another faith), devotees secretly carried the Krishna idol to Thrissur and entrusted it to the childless Kachanappilly (Kandanathu) Illam family; pleased by the couple's devotion, the lord took on his distinctive posture with a flute in one hand and the other outstretched. The present structure in traditional Kerala style is attributed to Sakthan Thampuran (Rama Varma), the Kochi ruler of the late 18th century who also founded the Thrissur Pooram. The temple's Bhadrakali shrine is associated with the Kodungallur Bhagavathy legend (the goddess is said to have arrived on the Namboodiri's umbrella), and the Bhagavathy is regarded as the younger sister of Paramekkavu Bhagavathy. The Thiruvambady Devaswom manages the temple today, and it stands as the chief rival of Paramekkavu in the Thrissur Pooram, famed for its Madathilvaravu procession to the Vadakkunnathan Temple.

name: Thiruvambady Temple
town_description: Thrissur, in central Kerala, is known as the cultural capital of the state, famed for the Thrissur Pooram festival, the Vadakkunnathan Shiva Temple around the Swaraj Round, and Kerala Kalamandalam (the classical arts university at nearby Cheruthuruthy). It is a major commercial and railway hub connecting northern and southern Kerala. The Thiruvambady Temple sits on Shoranur Road, about 1 km north of the Vadakkunnathan Temple.

travel.airport: Cochin International Airport (approx. 55 km; taxis and app cabs available).
travel.railway: Thrissur Junction (approx. 4 km); Punkunnam station is about 250 m from the temple.
travel.road: On Shoranur Road (Thrissur-Shornur Rd), Thiruvambady, Punkunnam, about 1 km north of the Vadakkunnathan Temple and 800 m from Swaraj Round (680022). City buses, autos and taxis ply the route; parking is difficult during peak festival times.

visitor_information.best_time: October to February for pleasant weather. Thrissur Pooram (April-May) is the most spectacular time to visit, but expect enormous crowds; weekday mornings are best for peaceful darshan.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning approx. 4:30 AM to 11:00 AM; evening approx. 5:00 PM to 8:30 PM (verify — sources vary: one listing says 4:00 AM-11:00 AM / 4:30 PM-8:30 PM, another 4:30 AM-12:00 noon / 5:00 PM-8:30 PM). The official temple site lists daily hours of 4:30 AM to 8:00 PM. Free lunch (annadhanam) is served to devotees daily; strict dress code applies.
